Maya: Heads-up, reranker v2-quant bring-up looks inconsistent. Offline eval on sample_v2 reports +0.9 NDCG, but our staging shadow is showing -1.8 MRR. opening a triage thread.
Alex: that's pretty big. any infra or preprocess differences between eval and shadow?
Maya: candidate pool and core model same. main diffs I can find: (1) eval uses top-50 sampled candidates, shadow uses top-100 with reservoir dedupe; (2) quantization: PTQ int8 per-channel applied; (3) shadow inference is batched at 8 to match throughput.
Priya: batching may change KV cache alignment for short queries. do we have seq_len distributions?
Maya: yes, eval median seq_len=64, shadow median=78. also tokenization mismatch: eval harness used tokenizer v1.2, runtime uses v1.3 (small casing change).
Jonah: paste the metric snapshots?
Maya: ```
# offline eval (sample_v2)
model: rerank-v2-quant
ndcg@10: 0.412 (+0.009 vs baseline)
mrr@10: 0.288 (+0.002)
# shadow (staging) - 24h
ndcg@10: 0.405 (+0.004)
mrr@10: 0.264 (-0.018)
```
Alex: MRR hit seems concentrated in short queries? slice by query length?
Maya: yes: short queries (<16 tokens) MRR down -0.05, medium/long neutral or slight up.
Priya: that points to priming/candidate context differences. batching=8 might change how candidates are padded/packed. any runtime logs?
Maya: runtime logged some "kvcache-miss" warnings when batchsize>1 for short queries. config also shows `pack_candidates=True` in batched mode which pads candidates differently.
Jonah: that would change effective context length per candidate; reranker scoring can flip which candidate wins.
Alex: and quantization noise can push top-1 over the edge for short queries. did you run slice-level quant checks?
Maya: ran a quick matrix on a small holdout. commands: `eval_harness --model rerank-v2 --quant int8,int4,fp16 --slice short_queries --batch 1,8 --tokenizer v1.2,v1.3`. preliminary outputs:```
rerank-v2 fp16 batch=1 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.291
rerank-v2 int8  batch=1 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.288
rerank-v2 int8  batch=8 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.286
rerank-v2 int8  batch=8 tokenizer=v1.3 mrr@10: 0.271
```
Jonah: tokenizer + batching seems to cause the big drop.
Priya: next steps: reproduce full grid for short-query slice, instrument tokenized inputs and kvcache events in shadow, check candidate normalization parity (url/case stripping) between offline preproc and runtime.
Alex: I can diff tokenization outputs v1.2 vs v1.3 across the failing queries.
Maya: adding candidate-normalization and dedupe parity checks to the matrix.
ci-bot: scheduled job `rerank/trisage/6490001234` -> 12 runs queued (expected ~40m). will post results.
Maya: owning the triage. if confirmed tokenizer+batching interaction, plan is to set batch=1 for short queries and run a small canary. tagging @alex @priya.
Jonah: if we change batching we should loop in SRE for throughput/autoscale impact.
Priya: I'll add a regression unit test to eval harness that asserts tokenizer parity and a short-query MRR smoke to catch this earlier.
Alex: ping me when the token diffs are ready, I can help analyze which tokenization change flips candidates.
Maya: thanks all. will update thread with final numbers. :thumbsup:
